goal: A flywheel validate (and fw validate) verb runs validate_task over every active task and exits non-zero naming each invalid task when any is statically invalid (exit 0 when all valid), and the orchestrator does not dispatch a statically-invalid task -- it surfaces the defect instead of running its agent.

relevant: packages/flywheel/src/flywheel/ -- the unified CLI shell (flywheel/fw console scripts and the verb router); add a `validate` verb that loads the active task set, runs validate_task per task, prints each invalid task + defects, and exits non-zero iff any task is invalid

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- the task selection/dispatch path; consult validate_task so a statically-invalid task is skipped-and-reported (mirroring how an unprovisionable task is skipped), never dispatched (D-3)
packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/__init__.py -- validate_task is consumed from here (produced by the prerequisite task)
references: packages/flywheel/src/flywheel -- existing verbs (status/next/init/...) show the router registration + exit-code conventions to mirror for `validate`
the defect record shape returned by validate_task (task_id + detail) is rendered identically by the verb and the orchestrator (spec shared invariant)
constraints: flywheel validate exits non-zero when >=1 active task is statically invalid and names each invalid task in its output; exits 0 when all are valid (criterion 4). fw validate is the same implementation, second entry point.
Schedule-time enforcement skips-and-reports an invalid task (does not dispatch its agent) and does not halt the whole worker for one bad task (D-3) -- one invalid task must not starve eligible peers.
Reuse validate_task from flywheel_core unchanged -- do not re-implement or weaken the validation logic here.
A pre-existing tasks tree with all-valid tasks behaves exactly as today (dispatch unchanged); only an invalid task changes behavior (skipped + reported).
Commit with a clear conventional-commit message; no emojis.
Run mcp__ide__getDiagnostics on every .py you touch and fix all Pylance errors before reporting done.
non_goals: Do not author, edit, weaken, delete, or read anything under .flywheel/holdout/00034-task-definition-validation/.
Do not change validate_task's signature or logic (owned by the prerequisite task).
Do not add execution/dry-run of graders.
Do not weaken existing CLI/router or workflow tests.
edge_cases: An active set with one invalid + one valid task: `validate` exits non-zero naming only the invalid one; the valid one is still dispatchable (criteria 3, 4).
An all-valid active set: `validate` exits 0; dispatch is unchanged from today.
An empty active set: `validate` exits 0 (nothing invalid).
notes: Criterion 4 (the verb exit code) is VISIBLE per spec 00034: the agent authors the verb test under packages/flywheel/tests (driving `flywheel validate` over a temp tasks tree, asserting non-zero exit + named invalid task on a mixed corpus and exit 0 on an all-valid one); the validate-verb-behavior grader runs it. The held-out integrity for spec 00034 lives in the validate-task oracle (the validation logic), consumed by the prerequisite task.
Surface layer; depends on the validation layer (spec Decomposition Hint).
